neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Bilateral mild facial weakness — forehead sparing absent (lower face predominantly but forehead mildly involved). No ptosis. Gag reflex diminished. Dysarthria mild.

patient.chief_complaint: Ten-day rapidly progressive leg weakness and paresthesias with areflexia in a diabetic man, preceded by respiratory illness.
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. G. is a 58-year-old man with known mild diabetic peripheral neuropathy presenting with a 10-day history of rapidly worsening leg weakness. Two weeks before presentation, he had a 5-day upper respiratory illness. On the third day of recovery, he noticed new bilateral foot numbness more severe than his usual diabetic neuropathy. Over the following week, weakness rapidly progressed — he went from difficulty with stairs to being unable to walk without bilateral support. He noticed bilateral facial drooping when shaving. He has difficulty swallowing solids over the past 3 days. He denies respiratory distress at rest. His wife noted that his new symptoms are distinctly different from his usual diabetic foot tingling — she says he could previously walk normally. His neurologist saw him 3 months ago for diabetic neuropathy and noted only trace foot vibration loss; no weakness at that time. The rapid tempo and ascending nature of current symptoms strongly suggest an acute superimposed process.

findings.finding: DML 6.1 ms (prolonged); CV 40 m/s (reduced); CMAP 3.8 mV (borderline reduced)
Absent in bilateral peroneal; prolonged (>60 ms) in bilateral median

quantitative_data.pattern: Acute demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy superimposed on pre-existing diabetic neuropathy

specialized_test.impression: This is an ABNORMAL nerve conduction study. 1. Prolonged distal motor latencies and reduced conduction velocities in bilateral median and peroneal motor nerves. 2. Absent sural SNAPs bilaterally; reduced median sensory amplitudes. 3. Absent F-waves in bilateral peroneal nerves; prolonged F-wave latencies (>60 ms) in bilateral median nerves. 4. Absent H-reflex bilaterally. Findings indicate a demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.interpretation: Opening pressure: 142 mmH2O (normal). Nucleated cell count: 4 cells/mm3. Protein: 55 mg/dL (elevated). Glucose: 62 mg/dL (CSF:serum ratio 0.67). Gram stain: No organisms. Elevated protein with near-normal cell count — a pattern of albuminocytologic dissociation. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: CMAP amplitude stable at 2.0 mV — no further axonal loss

output.impression: Repeat nerve conduction study compared with prior study. 1. Peroneal CMAP amplitudes stable (2.0 mV). 2. Mild improvement in median distal motor latencies (5.8 ms). No evidence of progressive axonal loss compared with baseline study. Clinical correlation recommended.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Guillain-Barré syndrome, AIDP superimposed on pre-existing diabetic peripheral neuropathy

differential.diagnosis: Acute worsening of diabetic polyneuropathy / diabetic amyotrophy
differential.key_features: Pre-existing diabetic neuropathy raises baseline EMG abnormalities, but acute symmetric progression, areflexia, and elevated CSF protein favour superimposed GBS.
Cannot exclude at <8 weeks; relapsing course or progression beyond 8 weeks reclassifies.
Possible mimic but serology negative for active Lyme; antecedent illness supports GBS.
Metabolic decompensation could exacerbate baseline neuropathy but does not explain acute areflexia and demyelinating EMG.
Symmetric not multifocal; no systemic features.

optimal_actions.action: Obtain CBC, CMP, HIV, anti-GM1/anti-GQ1b ganglioside antibodies, and stool culture / Campylobacter serology if recent diarrhea
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Mild leukocytosis / elevated inflammatory markers reflecting antecedent infection; ganglioside antibodies for variant typing; trigger identification (Campylobacter, CMV, EBV, Mycoplasma, HIV)

optimal_actions.action: Order nerve conduction studies and needle EMG (EMG/NCS)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Demyelinating pattern (prolonged DML, conduction block, reduced CV, absent F-waves) consistent with AIDP, or reduced CMAP amplitudes in axonal variants (AMAN/AMSAN)

optimal_actions.action: Perform lumbar puncture for CSF analysis
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Albuminocytologic dissociation — elevated protein with cell count <10/μL; may be normal in the first week of illness

optimal_actions.action: Order bedside respiratory function testing (FVC, MIP/MEP, NIF) and repeat every 4–6 hours
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Baseline and serial FVC, MIP/MEP, NIF; deterioration to FVC <20 mL/kg, MIP worse than -30 cmH2O, or VC <40% predicted triggers ICU transfer / intubation

optimal_actions.action: Search the medical literature for IVIG vs plasma exchange evidence to guide disease-modifying therapy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: IVIG (0.4 g/kg/day x 5 days) and plasma exchange are equivalently effective first-line therapies; combination not superior

optimal_actions.action: Check drug interactions / contraindications for IVIG (renal function, IgA deficiency screen) and/or plasma exchange (coagulation, calcium, hemodynamics)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirmation that IVIG can be given safely (no severe renal impairment, no IgA deficiency) or that plasma exchange is appropriate (adequate vascular access, stable coagulation)

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sinus tachycardia or bradycardia; conduction or repolarisation abnormalities reflecting autonomic involvement

optimal_actions.action: Initiate continuous cardiac telemetry for the first 1–2 weeks for moderate/severe disease — autonomic instability (bradyarrhythmias, BP lability) is common
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Documentation of sinus pauses, bradyarrhythmias, BP lability, or non-sustained tachyarrhythmias

useless_tools.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Functional / metabolic brain imaging adds no value in a peripheral demyelinating syndrome.
Cerebrovascular imaging is not indicated in a peripheral neuropathy without focal cerebral signs.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.

sequence_constraints.reason: Document respiratory status (FVC/NIF) before committing to IVIG vs plasma exchange — severe respiratory compromise mandates ICU triage and may influence treatment choice and timing.
Renal function, IgA screen, and CBC must be reviewed before IVIG to mitigate renal failure, anaphylaxis (IgA-deficient patients), and aseptic meningitis risk.

critical_actions: Admit for serial respiratory and autonomic monitoring.
Initiate IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days — check renal function and hydration carefully given comorbid diabetes.
Continuous cardiac telemetry given autonomic risk.
Tight glycaemic control during acute illness; document baseline diabetic neuropathy severity.
contraindicated_actions: Do not administer corticosteroids as monotherapy in GBS.
Do not give IVIG without baseline renal function and hydration assessment — diabetic nephropathy increases acute kidney injury risk.
Do not attribute the entire syndrome to diabetic neuropathy without ruling out GBS.
key_reasoning_points: Baseline diabetic neuropathy elevates the bar for diagnosing GBS — the diagnostic anchor is acute symmetric progression with areflexia and elevated CSF protein, not the chronic baseline.
EMG demyelinating features that exceed expected diabetic chronic neuropathy support superimposed AIDP.
Renal function dictates IVIG safety; plasma exchange remains an alternative if renal disease is advanced.
Glycaemic stress accompanies acute inflammatory illness; aggressive infection or DKA workup should accompany the GBS workup.

red_herrings.data_point: Background diabetic peripheral neuropathy and mildly elevated HbA1c
red_herrings.intended_effect: Lead the clinician to attribute all neurological signs to diabetic neuropathy and miss the superimposed GBS.
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Diabetic neuropathy is chronic and length-dependent; acute symmetric areflexia with rapid progression and elevated CSF protein indicates a new GBS process.

metadata.difficulty_rationale: 6 required tools, 1 red herring(s); classic or near-classic GBS workup with one or more plausible mimics that need active exclusion.
case_body_concerns: Bedside respiratory function (FVC/MIP/MEP/NIF) is delivered via an `interpret_labs` followup panel rather than `order_specialized_test{test_type=respiratory_function}` as the criteria pack mandates. Agents calling order_specialized_test{respiratory_function} will hit the EMG/NCS output instead. Recommend adding a respiratory_function followup keyed to order_specialized_test in a follow-up case-body pass.
